questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent a truck from rolling over?

options.text: Keep cargo as low as possible
Drive on the shoulder of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive on the shoulder of the road
questions.explanation: To prevent rollover, keep cargo weight low and drive slowly around turns. Driving on the shoulder does not help prevent rollover.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.explanation: Before driving, check all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, keep a following distance of at least ____ for every 10 feet of your vehicle length.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At higher speeds, add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: If you use the trailer hand brake while your trailer is skidding, it will:
questions.explanation: If your trailer is skidding, release the brakes to help tires regain traction. Using the trailer hand brake will only make the skid worse.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle is empty, the stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have:
questions.explanation: An empty vehicle stops more slowly than a loaded one. With less weight, the stiff springs and strong brakes have lower traction.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking
Should only be used for parking on downhill slopes
Should never be used for parking

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can release air pressure and let the brakes fail. Use the parking brake or wheel chocks instead.

questions.question: Keeping cargo low can:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too quickly. Keep the center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, you should:

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing

questions.explanation: If you must back on a curve, back toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure:
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost, the emergency trailer brakes activate automatically.

questions.question: To test the tractor protection valve, you should:

options.text: Release air by pressing the brake pedal

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, allow the air to charge, turn off the engine, then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure becomes unsafe.

questions.question: If your trailer drifts off-course while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift to correct it right away.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows a vehicle's wheels to lock up.
It stops a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
It makes turning a vehicle easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS helps stop wheels from locking up when you brake hard. If ABS finds a wheel about to lock, it reduces brake pressure to keep the wheel rolling.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Get out of the cab and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the cab and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, exit the vehicle immediately and walk away from the tracks. Then contact emergency services.

questions.question: If a parked trailer has no spring brakes, how do you keep it from moving?

options.text: Park it against a wall or another vehicle.
Park it on a slight slope.

questions.explanation: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, use wheel chocks to stop it from moving.

questions.question: If color-coded, what color identifies emergency or supply lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are color-coded to help drivers connect them correctly. Blue is for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: To test the trailer emergency brakes, place the air supply control in the "emergency" position and then:
questions.explanation: Before starting a trip, test the trailer emergency brakes. After checking that the trailer rolls freely, pull the air supply control to the "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly with the tractor to make sure the trailer does not move.

questions.question: If your trailer starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel left then right quickly.

questions.explanation: If your trailer begins to skid, release the brakes so the wheels can grip the road again. The trailer will straighten out once traction returns.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch the road ahead?

options.text: It is more dangerous than only watching your mirrors.
It does not help you drive more safely.
It helps you avoid sudden lane changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you avoid sudden lane changes.
questions.explanation: Looking down the road helps you see obstacles early. This way you can change lanes smoothly instead of making sudden, dangerous moves.

questions.question: When a trailer's wheels lock up, what can happen?

options.text: The trailer will be easy to drive.
The vehicle will keep steering control.

questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer can swing out and hit other vehicles. This risk is even higher with lightly-loaded trailers.

questions.question: Which trailer is most likely to roll over if you turn too quickly?
questions.explanation: Turn gently and smoothly when pulling trailers. Quick turns are dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.
